Unlike the maxillary first premolar, the pattern of grooves on the occlusal surface of the maxillary second premolar is more irregular and gives the tooth a “wrinkled” appearance.
Just as with the maxillary first premolar, the maxillary second premolar has a developmental depression evident on its mesial surface.

Statement 1: The mesial slope of the buccal cusp ridge of the maxillary first premolar is usually shorter than the distal slope. Statement 2: This is the opposite of the maxillary second premolar, where the mesial slope of the buccal cusp ridge is usually longer than the distal slope.
DAO Quiz 8 (Summer 2017): Statement 1 and 2 are true as written.
dao: Statement 1 is true while Statement 2 is false as written.
quiz: Statement 1 is false while Statement 2 is true as written.
column5: Statement 1 and 2 are false as written.
